songs_to_prepare.title: If I Loved You
songs_to_prepare.why: Romantic leading-man tenor/baritone with complex feelings — the conditional hypothetical of a doomed love

waitress/waitress-dr-pomatter.style_guidance: Dr. Pomatter is the awkward, well-meaning doctor who falls in love with his patient — tenor/baritone with natural warmth, an endearing nervousness, and genuine romantic quality. He is a good person doing a complicated thing.
avoid: Smooth, confident romantic lead — the whole point is his charming awkwardness, not polished seduction

songs_to_prepare.title: Master of the House
songs_to_prepare.why: The man who controls his environment through intimidation and genuine ownership of a small domain

songs_to_prepare.title: My Way
songs_to_prepare.why: If standards/pop accepted — the controlling man's credo, absolute and self-justifying

waitress/waitress-earl.style_guidance: Earl is the show's villain — baritone who is controlling, volatile, and dangerously ordinary. The performance must never play him as a cartoon; the horror is his complete sense of entitlement and self-justification.
avoid: Over-the-top villainy — Earl is terrifying precisely because he seems normal from the outside

songs_to_prepare.title: I Feel Pretty
songs_to_prepare.why: The person who is suddenly, gloriously in love and cannot contain it — tenor with complete, unbridled joy

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Pure theatrical energy — a man who has found his audience of one and is performing his entire soul for her

songs_to_prepare.title: Wonderful
songs_to_prepare.why: The enthusiastic man who genuinely loves something more than can be expressed in words — Ogie's brand of overwhelming presence

waitress/waitress-ogie.style_guidance: Ogie is the intensely, sincerely enthusiastic man who loves Dawn with his entire being immediately and forever — tenor/baritone with no restraint, zero self-consciousness, and such genuine warmth that his overwhelming nature becomes completely winning.
avoid: Comic irony or self-awareness about how much he is — Ogie is never joking. The comedy comes entirely from his absolute sincerity.

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Gruff authority figure who runs his domain with minimal emotional expression — baritone character with hidden warmth

songs_to_prepare.title: Sit Down, John
songs_to_prepare.why: The exasperated manager character — baritone who just wants everyone to do their job and stop with the feelings

waitress/waitress-cal.style_guidance: Cal runs the diner and pretends to be tougher than he is — baritone character voice with gruff warmth and the specific comedy of a man who cares deeply but is constitutionally unable to say so.
avoid: Warm, openly expressive material — Cal's entire personality is compressed warmth under deliberately indifferent surface

songs_to_prepare.title: Sunrise, Sunset
songs_to_prepare.why: The wise elder who has known love and loss — bass/baritone with earned warmth and the weight of years

songs_to_prepare.title: September Song
songs_to_prepare.why: The older man reflecting on time and the preciousness of what's left — bass-baritone warmth and wisdom

waitress/waitress-joe.style_guidance: Old Joe is the diner's secret heart — bass/baritone who has lived a full life, knows Jenna's worth, and whose relationship with her is the show's quiet emotional anchor. Age and warmth over vocal range.
avoid: Energetic or ambitious material — Old Joe's power is stillness, wisdom, and accumulated love

songs_to_prepare.title: What I Did for Love
songs_to_prepare.why: Contemporary mezzo-soprano with emotional specificity — the Waitress ensemble plays real people in a real small town

songs_to_prepare.title: She Used to Be Mine
songs_to_prepare.why: If auditioning for this specific show — shows the contemporary pop-musical voice the score requires

waitress/waitress-ensemble.style_guidance: Waitress ensemble plays the world of a small-town diner — contemporary pop-musical voices with warmth and specificity. This is not a dance-heavy show; strong acting through song and naturalistic presence matter most.
avoid: Showy or theatrical approach — this world is grounded and real; the magic is in the ordinary

songs_to_prepare.title: Somewhere Over the Rainbow
songs_to_prepare.why: Dorothy's defining moment — soprano/mezzo with lyrical warmth and the yearning of someone who wants to be somewhere other than here

songs_to_prepare.title: Part of Your World
songs_to_prepare.why: The girl who wants more than the world she knows — same yearning soprano quality, same emotional arc

songs_to_prepare.title: Wouldn't It Be Loverly
songs_to_prepare.why: The girl with a simpler dream — contrasting soprano/mezzo showing warmth and period-style charm

songs_to_prepare.title: Castle on a Cloud
songs_to_prepare.why: Soprano with longing and dream-quality — the girl imagining somewhere better, clear and focused

wizard-of-oz/dorothy.style_guidance: Dorothy needs a natural, warm soprano who makes 'Over the Rainbow' feel genuinely spontaneous — not a showcase, a moment of honest longing. The character is brave, curious, and thoroughly Kansas despite the extraordinary circumstances.
avoid: Belty pop approach — the Wizard of Oz calls for warm, lyric soprano quality; overdone technique undermines Dorothy's sincerity

songs_to_prepare.title: If I Only Had a Brain
songs_to_prepare.why: The Scarecrow's own song — shows the character's enthusiastic, physical, gentle comic quality

songs_to_prepare.title: Corner of the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: The person reaching for an identity they lack — baritone/tenor yearning for the ability to think

songs_to_prepare.title: Giants in the Sky
songs_to_prepare.why: The character discovering a whole world beyond what they knew — wide-eyed, physical, genuinely moved

wizard-of-oz/scarecrow.style_guidance: The Scarecrow is physical comedy first — rubbery, loose-limbed, endlessly enthusiastic. Baritone/tenor with comic timing, physical commitment, and the ability to make thinking itself look like a revelation.
avoid: Restrained physical performance — the Scarecrow's appeal is entirely in the specific, committed physical work

songs_to_prepare.title: If I Only Had a Heart
songs_to_prepare.why: The Tin Man's defining song — shows the tender, lyrical quality of a character who wants to feel

songs_to_prepare.title: This Nearly Was Mine
songs_to_prepare.why: Romantic baritone who thought he might get the thing he always wanted — warm, legit, genuine

songs_to_prepare.title: If I Loved You
songs_to_prepare.why: Baritone contemplating what love would feel like — the Tin Man asking the unaskable question in song

wizard-of-oz/tin-man.style_guidance: The Tin Man requires precise physical performance (rigid, joint-by-joint movement) combined with emotional longing — baritone with warmth who carries the show's most obviously human desire despite being made of metal. The contrast is the whole point.
avoid: Cold or mechanical vocal delivery — the Tin Man wants to feel; his singing should already be full of the emotion he claims not to have

songs_to_prepare.title: If I Were King of the Forest
songs_to_prepare.why: The Lion's fantasy anthem — baritone character who believes in his own imagined magnificence

songs_to_prepare.title: Adelaide's Lament
songs_to_prepare.why: The comedic character with anxiety as their dominant characteristic — physical, neurotic, entirely committed

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am What I Am
songs_to_prepare.why: Contrasting — where the Lion wants to go but can only get there in a fantasy sequence

wizard-of-oz/cowardly-lion.style_guidance: The Cowardly Lion is the show's biggest physical comedy role — baritone/character tenor with maximum range of expression (crying, boasting, hiding, roaring), specific physical work, and the genuine warmth of a natural protector who is terrified of himself.
avoid: Understated performance — the Lion operates in big, clear physical comedy; restraint is not in his vocabulary

songs_to_prepare.title: Rose's Turn
songs_to_prepare.why: The grande dame villain moment of reckoning — mezzo/alto with full theatrical power and a clear backstory of grievance

songs_to_prepare.title: I Know the Truth
songs_to_prepare.why: Dramatic mezzo confronting a situation she cannot change — the witch after Dorothy gets away

songs_to_prepare.title: The Witch's Rap / No Good Deed
songs_to_prepare.why: If a Wicked-influenced production — the villain's perspective, the mezzo with genuine grievance under the cackle

wizard-of-oz/wicked-witch.style_guidance: The Wicked Witch is one of musical theatre's most iconic villains — mezzo-soprano/alto with a cackle, genuine menace, specific physicality, and the theatrical authority to stop a show in its tracks. She needs both comedy and genuine threat.
avoid: One-note evil — the best Witches have a specific grievance and a real logic to their actions, even if the actions are terrible

songs_to_prepare.title: Glitter and Be Gay
songs_to_prepare.why: Operatic comedic soprano with self-aware glamour — Glinda's voice type and theatrical persona perfectly captured

songs_to_prepare.title: Popular

songs_to_prepare.title: I Feel Pretty
songs_to_prepare.why: Soprano with delight in her own perfection — Glinda before she has learned anything

wizard-of-oz/glinda.style_guidance: Glinda is the warm-hearted, comically self-certain good witch — soprano with sparkle, natural authority, and perfect pitch (literally and figuratively). She floats down in a bubble and nobody should doubt for a second that she is exactly as wonderful as she thinks she is.
avoid: Heavy or serious material — Glinda is radiant, light, and operates entirely at the level of reassuring certainty

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: The theatrical impresario running a show built on misdirection — character baritone with authority and charm

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am the Very Model
songs_to_prepare.why: The character claiming an expertise he entirely invented — patter baritone with pompous self-assurance

songs_to_prepare.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
songs_to_prepare.why: The character's own declaration of false omnipotence — if auditioning specifically for this production

wizard-of-oz/wizard.style_guidance: The Wizard is a con man with a good heart — character baritone with theatrical presence, charm, and the specific comedy of someone desperately trying to maintain a massive deception. He is warm, flustered, and entirely human.
avoid: Grand or actually intimidating baritone work — the Wizard deflates; the revelation of his smallness is the character's truth

wizard-of-oz/uncle-henry-auntie-em.role_name: Auntie Em / Uncle Henry / Miss Gulch / Glinda (touring double)

songs_to_prepare.title: So Big/So Small
songs_to_prepare.why: Maternal warmth and contained grief — Auntie Em's love for Dorothy in one song

songs_to_prepare.title: Sunrise, Sunset
songs_to_prepare.why: The warm adult who watches a child leave the world they tried to give them — mezzo-soprano with age and love

wizard-of-oz/uncle-henry-auntie-em.style_guidance: Em and Henry anchor the real world — warm, plain speaking character voices who make Oz genuinely extraordinary by contrast. In productions where they double as Oz figures (Witch/Omby), range and versatility matter.
avoid: Glamorous or theatrical material — Em and Henry are salt-of-the-earth Kansas; the ordinariness is the point

songs_to_prepare.title: Ding-Dong! The Witch Is Dead
songs_to_prepare.why: The Munchkins' celebration — shows ability to deliver high, bright ensemble tone with physical character work

songs_to_prepare.title: Be Our Guest
songs_to_prepare.why: Fantasy world ensemble who must be distinct characters with warmth and theatrical generosity

wizard-of-oz/ensemble.style_guidance: Wizard of Oz ensemble requires extreme character specificity — you may be a Munchkin, a crow, a apple-throwing tree, or a flying monkey. Strong physicality, character commitment, and the ability to shift between very different ensemble roles.
avoid: Generic ensemble approach — every creature in Oz has a specific physical and vocal character

songs_to_prepare.title: Finishing the Hat
songs_to_prepare.from: Sunday in the Park with George
songs_to_prepare.why: The scientist/artist consumed by his obsession — baritone explaining why the work means more than anything else

songs_to_prepare.title: Being Alive
songs_to_prepare.why: Mel Brooks's shows are Sondheim-adjacent in their emotional intelligence — baritone confronting what his obsession costs him

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: The Mel Brooks comedy baritone who commits completely to the premise — this is the tonal register Dr. Frankenstein lives in

young-frankenstein/dr-frederick-frankens.style_guidance: Frederick is the comic hero — baritone/musical comedy voice with intelligence, physical commitment to absurdity, and the ability to deliver Mel Brooks material with complete sincerity. He believes in his science completely, which is what makes it funny.
avoid: Ironic or winking performance — Mel Brooks comedy requires total commitment to the premise; Frederick is never joking

songs_to_prepare.title: The Music of the Night
songs_to_prepare.why: The isolated, misunderstood figure who wants to be seen as human — bass-baritone with power and yearning

songs_to_prepare.title: Something
songs_to_prepare.why: The Monster's awakening love — bass with unexpected tenderness under the physical imposing exterior

songs_to_prepare.title: Old Man River
songs_to_prepare.why: Deep bass-baritone with the weight of someone who exists outside normal human society — power and melancholy

young-frankenstein/the-monster.style_guidance: The Monster is a comic physical role first — bass-baritone who can also dance (he tap-dances in 'Puttin' on the Ritz') and deliver physical comedy while maintaining the character's genuine emotional arc. Voice ranges from grunts to full song; the contrast is the joke.
avoid: Pure horror — the Monster is sympathetic and comedic; the character wants connection and love, not dominance

songs_to_prepare.title: I Feel Pretty
songs_to_prepare.why: Sunshine soprano who is delighted by everything including her own existence — Inga's entire personality

songs_to_prepare.title: Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend
songs_to_prepare.why: Flirtatious, physically confident soprano with comic timing and charm — very Inga

songs_to_prepare.title: I Could Have Danced All Night
songs_to_prepare.why: Soprano who has discovered something wonderful — the joy and physicality of Inga's approach to the world

young-frankenstein/inga.style_guidance: Inga is the warm, enthusiastic, completely physical Swedish laboratory assistant — soprano belt with comic timing, willingness to lean into absurdity, and enormous charm. She is never an object; she drives her own story entirely.
avoid: Passive or objectified performance — Inga is active, joyful, and chooses everything she does

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: The comic sidekick who exists to make chaos and delight in it — character baritone at full commitment

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am the Very Model
songs_to_prepare.why: Hunchbacked character with a hump that moves — patter comedy delivered with total physical commitment

young-frankenstein/igor.style_guidance: Igor is the show's physical comedian — character baritone with a hunchback, a moving hump, and a completely individual interpretation of every social norm. The comedy is entirely physical and entirely committed. Igor knows he's funny; that is exactly the problem.
avoid: Subtle character work — Igor is broad, physical comedy delivered at maximum commitment in every scene

songs_to_prepare.title: Glitter and Be Gay
songs_to_prepare.why: The operatic comedic soprano who is obsessed with her appearance and absolutely committed to the bit — Elizabeth exactly

songs_to_prepare.title: Anything You Can Do
songs_to_prepare.why: The competitive soprano who must always win — Elizabeth's relationship with Frederick in one song

songs_to_prepare.title: Popular
songs_to_prepare.why: The woman entirely convinced of her own importance offering extremely unhelpful assistance — soprano comedy with self-unawareness

young-frankenstein/elizabeth-benning.style_guidance: Elizabeth is the comic-soprano fiancée obsessed with her hair — soprano/belt with operatic range, comic timing, and the specific comedy of someone who manages to make every situation about their own inconvenience. Mel Brooks comedy requires complete commitment to the bit.
avoid: Warm romantic soprano approach — Elizabeth is a comedy role; her relationship with Frederick is entirely secondary to hair maintenance

songs_to_prepare.title: I'm the Greatest Star
songs_to_prepare.why: Mezzo/alto character with enormous theatrical self-belief and the specific quality of someone who has been waiting a very long time for their moment

songs_to_prepare.title: Rose's Turn
songs_to_prepare.why: The veteran who has been waiting in the wings of someone else's story — alto/mezzo with theatrical power and dark comedy

songs_to_prepare.title: Whatever Lola Wants
songs_to_prepare.why: The woman who will not be denied and will use every tool available — character mezzo with predatory charm

young-frankenstein/frau-blucher.style_guidance: Frau Blücher causes horses to whinny merely by being named — alto/mezzo character with maximum theatrical presence, dark romantic obsession (for the old Dr. Frankenstein), and the specific comedy of complete, unwavering, completely inappropriate devotion.
avoid: Subtle or restrained performance — every entrance and exit Frau Blücher makes should be an event

songs_to_prepare.title: I Am the Very Model
songs_to_prepare.why: Military authority figure with a prosthetic arm — character baritone delivering pompous authority with physical comedy

songs_to_prepare.title: Sit Down, John
songs_to_prepare.why: The exasperated authority figure trying to maintain order amid increasing chaos — exactly Kemp's arc

young-frankenstein/inspector-kemp.style_guidance: Inspector Kemp has a prosthetic arm that takes on a life of its own — character baritone/bass with broad physical comedy, military swagger, and the ability to make a scene with a prop that is as much of a character as he is.
avoid: Subtle physicality — Kemp's prosthetic arm business must be fully committed, specific, and very, very funny

songs_to_prepare.title: Comedy Tonight
songs_to_prepare.from: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum
songs_to_prepare.why: Ensemble who must collectively create the comedy world — Mel Brooks requires total ensemble commitment to the bit

songs_to_prepare.why: The show's ensemble showstopper — if auditioning for this production, this is the number to understand

young-frankenstein/ensemble-young-franke.style_guidance: Young Frankenstein ensemble must be strong singers who can deliver Mel Brooks comedy with period musical-theatre style — the show is a loving parody of old-Hollywood monster movies and requires both the genre knowledge and the comedic commitment to fully land.
avoid: Contemporary pop style — this show lives in a very specific Mel Brooks / classic Hollywood / Golden Age musical parody space
